name: Commenda
key_source: Harris; vault qirad notes. Extended 2026-08-18: van Doosselaere 2009, 64-68 corroborates AP3, LR1, LR3, LR4, CF1, CF2 and LR6 on the Genoese corpus, and Harris 2007, 11 describes the arrangement in Hansmann-Kraakman-Squire terms as a separate asset pool with 'asymmetric owners' shielding and an asymmetric entity shielding'. TWO THINGS OUTSTANDING ON THIS ROW. (i) AP3=1 and LR1=limited may both be wrong: the traveller 'would bear sole liability toward third parties' (Harris 2007, 9) and his private assets are reachable by commenda creditors (11), so P is a candidate for AP3. Not changed in the batch that added the comparison form; see logbook 1, 2026-08-18. (ii) The row is coded on eleven of 32 characteristics and the entity questions - LP1-LP3, AP1, AP2, AP4, CI1-CI4 - are unasked, though Harris 2007, 11 and van Doosselaere 2009, 66 would now answer several. PAIRED WITH societas_maris, added 2026-08-18 and coded on the same eleven cells. This row covers the UNILATERAL form; the bilateral form is the other row. CF3=bilateral here means TWO PRINCIPALS and is not the literature's 'bilateral commenda' - see the societas_maris CF3 note.

name: Societas maris (the bilateral commenda; Venetian collegantia)
key_source: ADDED 2026-08-18 as a new type row - the code did not previously exist in this vocabulary, though it does in loss_mitigation_type.csv, where it is now coded. van Doosselaere 2009, 64-68: the Genoese notarial cartularies, 6,764 commenda ties 1154-1315, 93 per cent of all coded maritime ties. p.65 states the two liability rules side by side - the unilateral investor 'bore all liability for loss' and the traveller 'bore no capital risk', while in the bilateral form, 'often called SOCIETAS IN GENOA', 'the liability for loss was proportional to the respective initial investments'. Contribution ratio customarily one third traveller, two thirds investor; profit split equally. Harris 2007, 9-13; Held 2025, 22 for the Ragusan contracts sharing lucrum and damnum in the same proportions. CODED ON EXACTLY THE ELEVEN CHARACTERISTICS commenda CARRIES, so the pair is comparable cell for cell. It separates on two: LR6 (symmetric against upside-only) and CF1 (P against 1). It agrees on AP3, LR1, LR2, LR3, LR4, LR5, CF2, CF3 and TS2. DISSENT, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED: Pryor 1977, Luzzatto 1961, 119 and van Doosselaere 2009, 65 n.7 all hold unilateral and bilateral commenda to be 'essentially the same agreement', the choice turning on the traveller's wealth. Every one of them reaches that on the PAYOUT, where the economics are identical by construction (the arithmetic is at 65 n.6). None reaches it on the loss. The row is kept separate because both of this project's datasets measure the loss. PERIOD NOTE: loss_mitigation_type.csv gives '10-13c' for the same code. That is probably too early for the Genoese evidence, which van Doosselaere's corpus opens in 1154, and the two rows should be reconciled at review. CROSS-DATASET LINK, WHICH cooccurs_with CANNOT EXPRESS: the same code is coded in loss_mitigation_forms (RB1=RB2=shared). check_vocabularies.py normalises the '@dataset' suffix away and then reads societas_maris@loss_mitigation_forms as a self-reference, so the link is recorded here in prose instead. STILL WANTED: Lopez & Raymond 174-184, where the contracts are translated - it would supply the quoted clause van Doosselaere paraphrases. Coded 2026-08-18; see logbook 2 and logbook 4 for that date.

name: Mudaraba
key_source: NOT CODED HERE, AND THIS IS A DETERMINATION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION - the same disposition as ortoq_alloc in loss_mitigation_type.csv. Mudarabah is the HANAFI name for the institution coded in this dataset as 'qirad'. Ramli 2018, 97 on al-Sarakhsi's Kitab al-Mudarabah: al-Sarakhsi treats muqaradah as synonymous with mudarabah, 'the Malikites, Shafi'ites and Hanbalites unanimously use a different term i.e. qirad to denote such an activity', and 'in general, be it mudarabah, or muqaradah or qirad, it is by definition a commercial association whereby an investor or capital provider (rabb al-mal) entrusts some amount of capital to an agent... who trades with it and shares with the investor a pre-determined proportion of the profits'. Coding both rows would enter one institution twice and manufacture agreement between them on every cell. FALSIFICATION CONDITION, so this is not a permanent verdict. The schools are not known to diverge on any of the 32 characteristics, but one candidate is live and unverified: the vault note [[The mudaraba is revocable not locked in]] records that classical fiqh predominantly classifies the contract as an 'aqd ja'iz (revocable) while 'Maliki jurists restrict revocation once the agent has commenced work', flagged there as needing verification against fiqh sources. If that holds, mudarabah (Hanafi) and qirad (Maliki) separate on TS3 revocability - a WP2 capital-lock-in question, not a trivial one - and mudaraba earns a row. Note that qirad's own TS3 is currently uncoded, so the test cannot be run from what is in the matrix; it needs a Maliki source, which the library does not hold. Coded 2026-08-18; see logbook 2 and logbook 4 for that date.

name: Ortoq — equity regime (capital entrusted)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019 (Central Asian Survey 38:4, 10.1080/02634937.2019.1652799), 542-543, from Juvayni, Rashid al-Din and Vassaf. SPLIT from the generic 'ortoq' row: the type spans both values of AP3, CF2, LR1 and LR6, which one row cannot hold. Principal bears losses capped at his investment, agent bears none — the qirad/commenda configuration. NOT A PHASE: Enkhbold has loan financing adopted 'when Ogedei and Mongke ruled', i.e. contemporaneous with the equity examples from Ogedei's own reign, so equity and loan are COEXISTING CONTRACT TYPES whose relative prevalence shifted, not a sequence. Dates deliberately left unperiodised. NOT AN INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION from ortoq_loan — one institution, two contract forms; organizational_form_type.csv has no cooccurs_with column in which to say so.

name: Ortoq — loan regime (capital advanced at interest)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019, 543-544, on Allsen 1989 and Otagi 1973. The second half of the split: ortoqs 'completely liable for the loans they took, which extended beyond partnership capital to their private properties'; guarantors unconditionally bound; on default, seizure and then enslavement of the defaulter and his family (Rashid al-Din 1998, 726). The isqa configuration. Attested from Ogedei's and Mongke's reigns and 'eventually became prevalent... by the end of the thirteenth century'. Enkhbold's stated cause for the shift in prevalence: the government spent 76,000 ding of silver in 1240 bailing out ortoqs, and 'the huge losses suffered by Mongol elites motivated Mongol authorities to shift towards a risk-transfer model'. NOT AN INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION from ortoq_equity.

name: 合股 — silver share 銀股 (capital share in a Chinese partnership)
key_source: Zelin 2019 (Law and History Review 37:2, 10.1017/S073824801800038X), 337-350. SHARE CLASS, NOT FIRM: a single Qing partnership issued silver, body and dry shares simultaneously and they differ on CI3, AP3 and LR3, so the class is the coding unit. Entity-level characteristics (TS1, TS2, CI1, CI2, MG4) are coded HERE, on the partnership itself.

name: 身股 — body share (labour share, non-inheritable)
key_source: Zelin 2019, 345-346, citing Qingbai leichao and Morck & Yang on the Rishengchang bank. Dividends without equity; extinguishes at death into a term-limited 孤股. Coded WP2 and NOT as a pension: no fund, no contribution, no hazard — maintainer decision 2026-08-12.

name: 乾股 — dry share (contributed land, no loss liability)
key_source: Zelin 2019, 346. PARKED, NOT CODED. Holders at the Ruifeng ironworks outside Chongqing contributed the land on which the mine sat, took a proportional share of profits and were not held liable for losses — dormant-partner characteristics. One instance only; code when a second turns up.

name: 孤股 — death share (term-limited posthumous claim)
key_source: Zelin 2019, 346, via Morck & Yang. PARKED, NOT CODED. Kin of a deceased body-shareholder received a term-limited claim. Structurally life-contingent and comparable to widows_fund_scotland, but the only example is from the 1940s and Zelin flags that we do not know whether death shares were a product of foreign influence. Acquire Morck & Yang before coding.

name: 株 — local-market share (kabu nakama stock society)
key_source: Nagata 2008 (International Review of Social History 53:S16, 10.1017/S0020859008003635), 132-136. One share is a licence to operate one shop, mill or scale; the certificate for brewing stock was a wooden tag. The movement of shares outside the geographical region defined by the society was prohibited.

name: 株 — Edo export share (sake shipped to the Edo market)
key_source: Nagata 2008, 135. SPLIT from kabu_local: priced separately, and unlike the local shares these could be sold or traded outside the region or market of the original licence. Coded thinly; its value is the CI3 contrast.

name: 神會股 — share in a corporate deity association
key_source: Zelin 2019, 335-336, from Zhang, Annotated Compilation. Donors received shares commensurate with their endowment; rents fund ritual banquets and surplus is distributed to shareholders; shares sold irrevocably or on 典 dian redemption. Coded in BOTH censuses — see shenhui_gu_alloc@loss_mitigation_forms.
